record.tranche_reason: The study uses LRQP interventions in residual activations, rather than the original head-ablation method, and reports effects on IOI outputs and downstream attention patterns.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes in plots but gives no numerical effect sizes. It describes a true-value intervention as a control. It also summarizes probe results, which bear on IOI representations but do not test any listed version of the head circuit.
record.test_reason: The study uses LRQP, a probe-guided intervention, to flip the ABBA-vs-BABA variable in GPT2-small's residual stream at S2. This sits after the early heads and before the S-inhibition heads. It then measures the IOI logit difference, S-inhibition head outputs and name-mover attention. This is a different method aimed at the circuit's proposed information flow.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find an interpretable mid-network ABBA/BABA direction in one specific distribution. They show that LRQP interventions on it change downstream behaviour. They say this gives some evidence to support and slightly flesh out the IOI paper's account.
record.recipe_differences: Uses logistic-regression probes and LRQP residual-stream interventions, not the original head-circuit ablation and faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: ABBA vs BABA is linearly decodable at S2 from nearly all layers after the first attention layer. It is the top SVD direction from L5.mid to L8.mid.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT2-small's mid-layer residual stream at S2 has a dominant linear direction encoding IOI name order.

fits_no_version.finding: The positions of S1 and IO are probe-recoverable on clean IOI prompts but not with openwebtext prefixes. The authors say the prefixes broke several claims they had believed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Positional information in IOI representations is sensitive to prompt prefixing.

record.problems: Outcomes are described qualitatively without numerical effect sizes or uncertainty. The study uses one model and a specific prompt distribution. It does not directly ablate or patch circuit heads, and the authors note that Backup Name Mover behavior is inconsistent.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified outcomes for L7.pre are reported in the text. Figures are referenced, but no numerical figure values are present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: The 26-head count and all seven classes. The faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. Whether the output flip is mediated by name-mover attention; the authors list this as future work. No heads are ablated or patched directly.
Separate ABBA vs BABA outcomes. Template variation. Prompts with more names.
Not tested: no ablation of name movers.
Not tested as a comparison of circuit-finding methods.

missing.what: Probe results for S1 and IO positions: recoverable without prefixes, not with them. Relevant to prompt-distribution sensitivity.

record.verdict_notes: All results are qualitative and come from plots, with no numbers or uncertainty. I dropped the reader's V1 limits_scope label. 'Usually flipped' does not qualify V1. The Backup Name Mover inconsistency is expected under the original account, since backups engage mainly under name-mover ablation. V6 support is weak: it rests on a new prefixed format with orders pooled.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the 26-head count, all seven classes, or faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. It intervenes in the residual stream and measures some downstream head behavior, rather than intervening on the circuit heads.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.
Tests GPT2-small only; no other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics.
Does not compare ablation types or metrics, quantify sensitivity to prompt distributions, or test how much of the overall behavior the circuit explains.
Tests ABBA and BABA orderings, but does not separately compare templates or test prompts with more names.
